title: Why the LGPD Matters in UX Research
description: How Brazil's LGPD strengthens UX research: trust, answer quality and good practices for consent, data minimization and storage.

blocks.text: In user experience research, handling personal data is a central issue. Brazil's General Data Protection Law (LGPD) ensures data is collected ethically and securely, building participants' trust. Transparency and care in how data is used directly affect the quality of the answers and the reputation of companies.
How the LGPD Helps Build a Trustworthy Relationship with Users

The LGPD isn't just about meeting a legal obligation; it helps create a research environment where users feel their data is in good hands. That's essential at a time when people value privacy and digital security:

blocks.caption: Privacy handled well improves the quality of the research.

items: Building Trust: being transparent about how data is used strengthens the relationship with participants. When they know their data will be handled responsibly, users feel safer answering honestly.
Quality of Information: confident participants tend to give more detailed and honest answers, raising the quality of the design decisions based on that information.

blocks.text: Best Practices for Applying the LGPD in UX Research
To make data collection safer and LGPD-compliant, it's important to adopt practices that ensure security and respect for the user:

blocks.caption: The article's best practices as a checklist.

items: Clear Information and Informed Consent: clearly explain the goals of the research and the purpose of each piece of data you ask for. Make sure participants understand how and for how long their data will be used before they consent.
Data Minimization: ask only for information that's essential to the research. Collecting the minimum data necessary is one of the best ways to avoid potential security and compliance problems.
Data Storage and Protection: the personal data collected must be stored securely. It's also important to set deadlines for deleting the data, giving participants security and peace of mind.

blocks.text: Today it's common to transcribe interviews and analyze answers with AI tools. That saves time, but it raises a new question: where is the participants' data going?

items: State in the consent form whether recordings or transcripts will go through third-party tools.
Remove names, contact info and any identifiable data before sending the material for analysis.
Prefer tools with a contract that prohibits using the data to train models.
Define how long the material is kept and dispose of it afterwards.

blocks.caption: Personal data comes out before any external tool. For the analysis, P07 is worth as much as the real name.

blocks.text: Data Protection as a Pillar of Credibility

By following the LGPD's principles, companies don't just meet legal requirements, they also strengthen their image. Attention to privacy becomes a competitive advantage, since reliability and respect for the user become evident.
In short, bringing the LGPD into UX research contributes to a more transparent and respectful relationship, and offers an experience where participants feel safe and valued.
